name: SENTINEL electricity attack-screening model (compact Random Forest, load-invariant features)
intended_use: Advisory screening of benchmark power-system measurements for cyber-physical attack signatures; raises investigation priority. High precision, low coverage.
not_intended_for: declaring that an attack did or did not occur
assuring a grid is safe when no flag is raised
warning: Advisory screening only. On held-out benchmark data this model flagged about 40% of attack observations (recall 0.396); a missing flag never means the grid is safe. A flag is evidence to investigate, not proof of an attack, compromise or outage.

source.dataset: MSU-ORNL Power System Attack Datasets (three-class release, 'triple')
source.authors: Uttam Adhikari, Shengyi Pan, Tommy Morris (Mississippi State University) with Raymond Borges and Justin Beaver (Oak Ridge National Laboratory)
source.citation_hint: Pan, Morris, Adhikari, IEEE Trans. Smart Grid (doi:10.1109/TSG.2015.2409775) and related papers listed on the landing page
source.nature: Simulated benchmark of a two-generator, two-line, four-IED transmission test system; 1% random samples; no timestamps. Not SENTINEL city telemetry.

decision_rule: predict Attack if P(Attack) >= tau; otherwise argmax(P(NoEvents), P(Natural))
tau_source: grouped out-of-fold predictions inside train files data1-9, lowest tau with <= 10% natural->attack

features.definition: src/invariant.py (row-wise ratios: sequence components, phase unbalance, per-phase vs positive sequence, frequency deviation, df/dt, impedance angle/infinite flag, relay status, logs)

limitations: About 60% of attack observations are not flagged (held-out recall 0.396); most are classified as natural disturbances
A 'normal' prediction is only 0.54 precise on held-out data; never present it as 'no attack'
Single 1% snapshots without timestamps or command context; attacks designed to mimic natural faults are hard to separate
One benchmark system (2 lines, 4 IEDs) and 37 scenario types; no evidence for unseen attack types or other grids
About 7-9% of natural disturbances are flagged as cyberattacks (designed cap 10%)
Explanations are model feature influence (tree-path contributions), not causal attribution
explanations: Feature influence = this model's additive contribution to P(cyberattack) for this sample. It shows what drove the score, not what caused any event.
